title: Half-hidden Quagmire IV: one dictionary keyword alphabet (666,993 incl. transposition-mixed), the other alphabet anything; repeating key of 1-12 unknown numbers or sliding key (running sum of an unknown word) of 1-9
k4_result: 316,154,682 settings (666,993 alphabets x 2 sides x (12 repeating key lengths + 9 sliding lengths x 25 word sums); Vigenere and Beaufort form are one test here). 0 settings pass with 5+ checks. 5 survivors in all, all with the cipher alphabet hidden and key length 8: 2 repeating (4 checks; chance expects about 0.1) and 3 sliding (3 checks; chance expects about 2.7). All five read as noise after the hidden alphabet is completed on the big English model: -6.11, -6.27, -6.31, -6.46, -6.52 per quadgram (English needs -5.1; planted answers read -4.2 to -4.8). Repeating key: for 19 of the 24 (side, length) cells no alphabet of any kind can close the loops (cipher side hidden: every length 1-12 except 8; plain side hidden: 1-7 and 9), a fact about K4's clue letters alone; plain side hidden at 10, 11, 12 has 362, 800 and 1,332 alphabets that close the loops but every one puts two letters on one place. So length 8 is the only repeating key where the dictionary matters. Sliding key lengths 1-7 and 9: 0 survivors.
controls: 3 shuffled K4s, each on all 666,993 alphabets: 0 passes with 5+ checks in each. Survivors 93, 15,535 and 2 (almost all at repeating lengths 10 and 12, where a shuffled text is not blocked the way K4 is; at key length 8: 11, 168 and 2). Best completed readings -6.04, -5.80, -6.36: noise, and two of the three read better than K4's best (-6.11).
scope_limits: The known alphabet must be one of 666,993: A-Z, KRYPTOS, a dictionary keyword alphabet or its two transposition-mixed forms; decimated or reversed dictionary alphabets, non-dictionary keywords and both alphabets hidden are not covered (the last is the known open gap). Key: a repeating key of 1-12 or the running sum of a word of 1-9, any numbers. Only the decided cells are solid: a repeating key of 1-7 or 9-12 is impossible for K4 whatever the known alphabet is; at length 8 and for sliding keys of 3-9 the result holds for the listed alphabets only. Sliding length 9 with the cipher side hidden has just 2 checks (961 loop fits, all with colliding letters). Key lengths 13+ are not run (0-1 checks). The clue positions are taken as exact. Survivors of the shuffled texts beyond the best 20 got only a quick annealing pass (2,500 steps), which can miss a weakly forced long-key system; all 5 of K4's survivors got the long pass (6 x 20,000 steps). The 'chance expects' figures assume a random known alphabet and are rough.

negative.hypothesis: K4 is a Quagmire IV with a short key in which one alphabet comes from a dictionary keyword and the other was written down freely (Sanborn's change 'so that Scheidt could not decipher it').
negative.scope: 666,993 known alphabets (A-Z, KRYPTOS, dictionary keyword alphabets and their two transposition-mixed forms) on the plain side with a fully hidden cipher alphabet, and on the cipher side with a fully hidden plain alphabet; repeating key of 1-12 unknown numbers, and sliding key (running sum of an unknown word) of 1-9 with every word sum; Vigenere and Beaufort form; exact loop checks on the 24 clue letters plus distinct places for the hidden letters; survivors completed by annealing on the big English model; 316,154,682 settings.
negative.outcome: Dead in scope: 0 settings with 5+ checks; 5 chance-level survivors at key length 8 (2 repeating, 3 sliding; about 2.8 expected), all noise, best -6.11 per quadgram against -5.1 needed (controls: 3 shuffled K4s on all alphabets, 0 passes with 5+ checks, 2-15,535 survivors, best readings -6.04, -5.80, -6.36; planted 9/9, read back 82-97 of 97 letters at -4.2 to -4.8). A repeating key of 1-7 or 9-12 is impossible for any known alphabet at all.

follow_ups: Both alphabets hidden at key length 8, the one short repeating key that K4's clue letters do not block: there the cipher letters fall into two pieces (11 and 3 letters) with 4 loop checks on the plain alphabet. Each check is a +-1 sum of 6-8 plain-letter places, so the plain alphabet can be searched by the checks themselves: enumerate places for the 13 clue plain letters that close all 4 loops (26^9 after the checks, far fewer with distinct places and pruning loop by loop), and score each by the 54 forced plaintext letters on the big model. Planted: random alphabets on both sides, key length 8.

Sliding key with the word sum W = 13 or an even W is special: the key repeats after 2L or 13L letters. The 26 collide-only fits at sliding length 8 (cipher side hidden) could be re-read allowing ONE clue letter to be wrong, as idea 81 did for the key-rule battery; cost is 24 times this run, about 5 minutes.

The same half-hidden test with a decimated dictionary alphabet on the known side (place x multiplied by 3, 5, 7, 9, 11: Sanborn 'skipping' through his keyword alphabet). It is this script with 5 more copies of the alphabet list; only key length 8 and the sliding keys need it.
